Summary

Encrypted traffic recorded today can be decrypted later if the key exchange that protected it is broken by a quantum computer. A hybrid post-quantum key exchange such as X25519MLKEM768 closes that gap, and every current browser offers one. This report measures every week which Dutch websites accept it: the .nl domains in the Tranco top 1 million and curated lists of banks, government bodies, hospitals and web shops, 9 domains in total.

  1. 40.0% (95% CI 11.8–76.9%) of the 5 reachable .nl domains in the Tranco top 250,000 use post-quantum key exchange by default.
  2. Cloudflare alone hosts 100.0% of all post-quantum domains; the three networks with the most post-quantum domains together host 100.0%.
  3. 20.0% of reachable domains negotiate TLS 1.2 with a current browser, which rules out the hybrid key exchange.

3Sectors

4Hosting networks

A content delivery network terminates TLS for the sites it serves, so its configuration decides the key exchange for all of them. Cloudflare alone hosts 100.0% of all post-quantum domains; the three networks with the most post-quantum domains together host 100.0%.

5Protocol

The hybrid groups are only defined for TLS 1.3, so a server that negotiates TLS 1.2 cannot use them. Table 1 lists the group each server chose in the default handshake, Table 2 the TLS version.

6Coverage

1 of the 6 domains in the Tranco top 250,000 (16.7%) did not complete a TLS handshake on port 443, on the domain or its www host. They are left out of every percentage.
